title: Back-rank safety
objectives: Recognize when a castled king has no escape from a check along its own back rank
Create luft (an escape square) before a back-rank checkmate is forced

steps.text: A castled king boxed in by its own untouched pawns can be checkmated by a single rook or queen reaching the back rank — the king simply has nowhere to go. This is exactly what just happened here: White's king has no escape square, so ...Re1 isn't just check, it's checkmate.

steps.prompt: One move earlier: White's king has no escape square, and Black threatens ...Re1#. Give your king an escape square (create "luft") before it's forced on you.

hints.text: Nothing defends White's back rank, and Black threatens ...Re1# next move.
Look at your king's own pawn shield — moving one of those pawns opens an escape square.
Push a kingside pawn one square.
h3 gives the king a square to step to — now a back-rank check is just check, not mate.

feedback.default: That doesn't fix the back-rank problem — the king still has no escape square if a rook or queen reaches the back rank. Move a kingside pawn to open an escape hole.

steps.successExplanation: Moving a kingside pawn opens an escape square for the king — now if a rook reaches the back rank, it's check, not checkmate.

steps.prompt: Which of these actually prevents a back-rank checkmate?
options: Keeping your rook on the back rank
Giving your king an escape square by moving a pawn off its second rank
Castling earlier in the game, no matter what

feedback.default: That doesn't address a boxed-in king directly. The fix is giving the king somewhere to go — "luft."

steps.successExplanation: Right — an escape square (luft) means that even if a rook or queen reaches your back rank, it's check, not checkmate.

steps.summary: A castled king with an untouched pawn shield can be mated by a single rook or queen reaching the back rank. Make a habit of asking: if a rook landed on my back rank right now, does my king have anywhere to go? If not, spend a move creating luft before it's forced on you.
